claim: On Wednesday 22 May 2024, then-PM Rishi Sunak announced a general election, speaking outside 10 Downing Street in heavy rain [00:00]
quote: on Wednesday the 22nd of May 2024 then prime minister rishy sunak walked out that front door and announced that he was calling a general election
evidence: CNN and Deadline both confirm Sunak announced the 4 July 2024 election on 22 May 2024 outside No.10, soaked by rain.

claim: A protester outside Downing Street played D:Ream's 'Things Can Only Get Better' during Sunak's election announcement — a song used as Labour's 1997 election anthem [00:00]
quote: a protester in the adjoining Street had set up a PA system and started blasting things can only get better a song by one hit wonders Dam which had previously been used as an election Anthem by the labor party
evidence: Multiple outlets confirm a protester blasted D:Ream's song, Labour's 1997 campaign anthem, during the speech.

claim: The Conservative Party had governed the UK for 14 years by the time of the 2024 general election [01:02]
quote: the conservative party whose 14-year rule over the UK
evidence: Cameron's coalition took office 11 May 2010; the 2024 election was called 22 May 2024 — just over 14 years of continuous Conservative-led government.

claim: As of 2024, the UK has the highest house price-to-income ratio since the Victorian era [01:02]
quote: the highest housing to income ratio since the Victorian era
evidence: ii.co.uk (2024): average UK home costs ~9x earnings, described as the highest ratio since Victorian times (when the ratio was actually higher, ~12x, so the claim reads as 'highest of the post-Victorian era'). Best reachable sources are financial-commentary sites rather than an ONS/academic study that itself makes the Victorian comparison, capping the verdict at plausible.

claim: David Cameron became UK Prime Minister on 11 May 2010, after the Conservatives won 306 seats — 20 short of a majority — in that year's general election [02:33]
quote: the conservatives have only managed to win 306 seats in the House of Commons that's 20 seats short of an outright majority
evidence: Conservatives won 306 of 650 seats in 2010, 20 short of the 326 needed for a majority — exact match.

claim: The Cameron-Clegg coalition, formed after 5 days of negotiations in May 2010, was the UK's first coalition government since the cross-party National Government of the 1930s-40s [03:10]
quote: after 5 days of negotiations Cameron and CLE have agreed to form a coalition government…the last time this happened was during the 1930s and 1940s when all the major parties in Parliament came together
evidence: Cameron-Clegg coalition formed 11 May 2010, 5 days after the election; it was the UK's first coalition since the National Government of 1931-40, which itself governed into the wartime period.

claim: As Prime Minister, David Cameron pushed for the UK to legalize same-sex marriage despite opposition from many of his own Conservative MPs [04:15]
quote: he'll soon push for the UK to adopt equal marriage despite solid opposition from other conservatives
evidence: The May 2013 Commons vote passed 400-175, but only 127 of 303 Conservative MPs backed it — 136 voted against, confirming solid intra-party opposition to a Cameron-backed bill.

claim: In the aftermath of the 2008 financial crisis, the UK government effectively nationalized two banks and bought significant ownership stakes in two more [05:19]
quote: the previous government has paid to effectively nationalize two Banks and shouted out to buy significant ownership stakes in two more
evidence: Northern Rock and Bradford & Bingley were taken into full public ownership; the government took a ~70-84% stake in RBS and a large minority stake (~40%) in Lloyds Banking Group — two full nationalisations, two large stakes.

claim: Labour's outgoing Chief Secretary to the Treasury, Liam Byrne, left a handwritten note for his successor in May 2010 reading 'I'm afraid there is no money. Best regards and good luck' [05:19]
quote: dear Chief secretary I'm afraid there is no money best regards and good luck
evidence: Byrne's May 2010 note to successor David Laws is well documented and was later waved by Cameron at campaign events, as the video also states.

claim: In 2010, the incoming UK government inherited a budget deficit of around £150 billion [06:22]
quote: the UK government is running a budget deficit of 150 billion
evidence: The June 2010 Budget cited a deficit outturn of around £149-156bn depending on the measure used — closely matching '150 billion'.

claim: In 2010, UK interest rates were at their lowest since 1694 [06:22]
quote: interest rates are at their lowest since 1694
evidence: Bank rate was cut to 0.5% in March 2009, widely reported as the lowest in the Bank of England's history since its founding in 1694.

claim: The Cameron government's 2010 spending review cut funding for schools and colleges by (as transcribed) '133%' [06:22]
quote: a 133% cut in funding for schools and colleges
evidence: A 133% cut is mathematically impossible, so this is almost certainly an auto-caption misrendering of a smaller figure (most plausibly '13%'). Documented cuts: school sixth-form funding per student fell ~10% by 2014/15 (26% by 2018/19); FE/sixth-form college funding fell ~18-33% depending on sub-sector and period. A low-teens percentage reading sits within the real range even though the number as spoken cannot be literal.

claim: The Cameron government's 2010 spending review cut university (higher education) funding by 40% [06:22]
quote: a 40% cut to funding for universities
evidence: The 2010 Comprehensive Spending Review cut the HE resource budget (excl. research) from £7.1bn to £4.2bn by 2014-15 — a 40% reduction, matching the claim exactly.

claim: University tuition fees in England were tripled, shifting the funding burden onto students [06:22]
quote: made up for by Shifting the burden of tuition costs onto students through a tripling of fees
evidence: The fee cap rose from £3,290 to £9,000 from 2012 — a ~2.7x rise, commonly and reasonably described as a tripling.

claim: Public sector workers had pay frozen for two years from 2010, with subsequent annual pay rises capped at 1% [06:22]
quote: anyone working in the public sector has their pay Frozen for 2 years and subsequent annual pay Rises capped at 1%
evidence: Public sector pay was frozen for two years from 2010, then capped at 1% annual rises from 2013 — matches the claim (the video omits the 2010-2013 gap between the freeze and the formal 1% cap).

claim: The Royal Mail was privatized in 2013 and sold to investors at what has been characterized as a bargain-basement price [07:28]
quote: the Royal Mail the UK's postal service is sold off to investors at a Bargain Basement price
evidence: NAO found the October 2013 sale was priced too cautiously — shares priced at 330p closed 38% higher on day one, an estimated up to £2.3bn lost to taxpayers.

claim: By 2015, the UK budget deficit had dropped by more than a third from its 2010 level [07:28]
quote: by 2015 the deficit has dropped by more than a third
evidence: Public sector net borrowing fell from a peak of £157.7bn (FY2009-10) to £87.3bn (FY2014-15) — a ~45% fall, comfortably more than a third.

claim: Corporation tax was gradually cut from 28% to 20% by 2015 [08:32]
quote: corporation tax the tax paid by companies on their profits is gradually brought down from 28% to just 20% by 2015
evidence: Main rate cut in stages from 28% (2010/11) to 20% (2015/16) — exact match.

claim: The UK's most prominent food bank charity distributed about 40,000 parcels in 2010, rising to more than 1 million by 2015 [08:32]
quote: the country's most prominent Food Bank charity had handed out just 40,000 packages that entire year but but by 2015 that figure has risen to more than 1 million
evidence: Trussell Trust distributed 40,898 parcels in 2009-10 and 1,084,604 in 2014-15 — matches the claim almost exactly.

claim: Labour led the Conservatives in opinion polls from late 2010 through most of the following four years, but the Conservatives still increased their seats from 306 to 331 in the 2015 general election [09:36-10:42]
quote: by the end of 2010 the labor party has overtaken Cameron's conservatives in the polls a lead they maintain consistently for the next four years…their 306 MPS have become 331
evidence: Labour led most polls 2011-2014 (e.g. 44%-31% July 2012, a 19-point lead March 2013), narrowing to ~2pts by late 2015. The Conservatives won 330-331 seats in 2015 (sources differ by one depending whether the Speaker is counted) — up from 306.

claim: Net migration to the UK from other EU member states had been trending further and further upwards since the early 2000s [11:48]
quote: since the early 2000s net migration to the UK from within the EU has been trending further and further upwards
evidence: Net EU migration rose sharply after the 2004 enlargement (from ~10k/yr to ~100k/yr) but then plateaued 2004-2009 before rising again toward the 2016 referendum — the direction is right but 'further and further' overstates the smoothness of the trend, which had a multi-year plateau.

claim: Research indicates net EU migration has had a positive impact on the UK economy [11:48]
quote: all of the available research suggests that this has a positive impact on the UK economy
evidence: UCL/CReAM research: EU-15 migrants contributed 64% more in tax than they received in benefits (2001-2011); A10 migrants 12% more; other studies found no negative wage effect on UK-born workers in high-migration regions.

claim: David Cameron made high-profile promises to bring net migration down into the 'tens of thousands' [12:52]
quote: making high-profile promises to bring net migration down into the tens of thousands
evidence: Cameron pledged in 2010 to reduce net migration to the 'tens of thousands'; the pledge was never met and net migration hit 260,000-333,000 in 2014-15.

claim: In 2014, one of David Cameron's own Conservative MPs defected to UKIP [12:52]
quote: in 2014 one of Cameron's own MPS even defects to the party
evidence: Douglas Carswell defected from the Conservatives to UKIP on 28 August 2014, triggering the Clacton by-election.

claim: The available evidence at the time suggested staying in the EU was the more prosperous economic choice for the UK [13:55]
quote: all the available evidence suggests that staying a member of the European Union is the more prosperous economic choice for the UK
evidence: HM Treasury's pre-referendum analysis projected leaving would leave households worse off by £1,800-£4,300/yr depending on scenario. This is a primary document, but it was produced by the government of a sitting, Remain-campaigning PM, so it is not a neutral party — later independent analyses broadly corroborated a negative growth effect from leaving, though magnitudes differ, which caps this at plausible rather than confirmed.

claim: The BBC announced Britain had voted to leave the EU at 4:40am on 24 June 2024 [as stated in the transcript] [14:58]
quote: at 4:40 a.m. on the 24th of June 2024 the BBC announces that Britain has voted to leave the European Union
evidence: The BBC forecast the Leave result just before 4:40am BST on 24 June 2016 — not 2024, an 8-year discrepancy. This is very likely a speech-to-text misrendering of '2016' (the rest of the video's own chronology — Cameron's resignation, May's 2016-19 premiership, Johnson's 2019 election — only makes sense with a 2016 referendum), but as transcribed the claim states a year that is flatly wrong.

claim: Theresa May became Prime Minister after David Cameron's resignation, with Boris Johnson pulling out of the Conservative leadership contest [16:31]
quote: he bottles it at the last minute and the leadership contest is won instead by this woman Theresa May
evidence: Johnson withdrew from the July 2016 leadership race after losing key support; May became party leader and PM on 13 July 2016.

claim: Theresa May called a snap 2017 election hoping to increase her majority, but the Conservatives lost seats instead, forcing her to form a confidence-and-supply pact with the DUP [17:35-18:40]
quote: May doesn't secure the increased majority she expected but loses seats instead Clinging On to power thus requires her to form a pact with the right-wing Democratic unionist party
evidence: Conservatives won 318 seats in 2017 (down from 330), losing their majority, and signed a confidence-and-supply deal with the DUP's 10 MPs.

claim: Theresa May told an ITV interviewer that the naughtiest/most rebellious thing she had ever done was run through a field of wheat [18:40]
quote: she tells a reporter from ITV that the most rebellious thing she's ever done is run through a field of wheat
evidence: In an ITV 'Tonight' interview with Julie Etchingham on 5 June 2017, May said running through fields of wheat as a child was the naughtiest thing she'd done.

claim: Theresa May's Brexit withdrawal agreement was rejected by Parliament in three separate votes before she resigned [19:44]
quote: after three failed attempts to get her agreement through Parliament May decides that she's had enough
evidence: Three 'meaningful votes' on May's deal were held and lost, on 15 Jan, 12 Mar, and 29 Mar 2019, before she announced her resignation two months later.

claim: Boris Johnson officially became Prime Minister on 24 July 2019 [20:47]
quote: officially takes over as prime minister on the 24th of July 2019
evidence: Johnson won the Conservative leadership contest (announced 23 July 2019) and became PM on 24 July 2019 — exact match.

claim: In August 2019, Boris Johnson prorogued (suspended) Parliament for about a month, and the Supreme Court later ruled the suspension unlawful [20:47]
quote: Johnson takes the extreme decision to drive to Buckingham Palace and to persuade the queen to effectively suspend Parliament for a month…the Supreme Court rules his suspension of parliament to have been illegal
evidence: Johnson sought a 5-week prorogation in late August 2019; the Supreme Court ruled unanimously on 24 Sept 2019 that the suspension was unlawful and void.

claim: In the December 2019 general election, Boris Johnson's Conservatives won a landslide of 365 seats to Labour's 203 [21:49]
quote: Johnson secures a landslide Victory with 365 seats to labors 203
evidence: Conservatives won 365 seats, Labour 203, in the 12 December 2019 election — exact match.

claim: The first two COVID-19 cases in Britain were documented on 30 January 2020 [22:53]
quote: on the 30th of January 2020 the first two cases of covid-19 are documented in Britain
evidence: Most accounts, including the Chief Medical Officer's own confirmation, date the first two confirmed UK cases to 31 January 2020 — one day after the claim's date. A minor, likely off-by-one discrepancy rather than a substantive error.

claim: Boris Johnson announced a nationwide lockdown on 23 March 2020, having earlier considered allowing the disease to spread to build 'herd immunity' [22:53]
quote: on the 23rd of March Boris Johnson appears on national TV to announce a nationwide lockdown…he briefly considered actively allowing the disease to spread across the country to build so-called herd immunity through infection
evidence: UK's initial strategy pursued controlled spread toward herd immunity before reversing to a lockdown announced 23 March 2020, as the exponential case rise made the earlier approach untenable.

claim: Boris Johnson was hospitalized and moved to intensive care at St Thomas' Hospital after contracting COVID-19 [23:55]
quote: lying in an intensive care unit in St Thomas Hospital
evidence: Johnson was admitted to St Thomas' Hospital 5 April 2020 and moved to ICU on 6 April, spending three nights there.

claim: Dominic Cummings was found to have broken lockdown rules by driving roughly 5 hours to Durham to see his family while showing COVID symptoms [23:55]
quote: Dominic Cummings gets caught out for having broken lockdown Rules by visiting his wife 5 hours away whilst displaying covid symptoms
evidence: Cummings drove 264 miles from London to Durham on 27 March 2020 (a 4-5 hour drive, matching '5 hours away'); Durham Police later concluded a subsequent Barnard Castle trip would have warranted police intervention.

claim: During the pandemic the government suspended normal anti-corruption safeguards for procurement, and billions of pounds went to associates of ministers via a fast-track 'VIP lane,' in some cases for equipment that proved unusable [23:55]
quote: Johnson and Co thus leverage this urgency to suspend anti-corruption laws around government Outsourcing billions of pounds worth of public money is handed over to the friends and acquaintances of government ministers in some cases in return for equipment which is entirely unusable
evidence: ~£3.8bn was spent via a VIP fast-track lane routing PPE offers from ministers, officials and MPs (many Tory-linked); a London court ruled the lane unlawful; NAO found large volumes of unsuitable PPE, with total write-offs approaching £10bn.

claim: The 'Eat Out to Help Out' scheme in August 2020 subsidized around 160 million meals [24:59]
quote: gobbling up 160 million State subsidized meals between them
evidence: Official statistics: £849m claimed across 160 million individual meals (covers) at 78,116 outlets — exact match.

claim: A study found the Eat Out to Help Out scheme contributed to a near doubling of COVID-19 cases during that month [24:59]
quote: sunx scheme contributes to a near doubling of cases during that month
evidence: The actual causal study (Fetzer, Warwick CAGE, Oct 2020) attributes 8-17% of new infection clusters emerging in August/September to the scheme — a real and policy-relevant effect, but far short of 'a near doubling of cases', which overstates the magnitude the underlying research found.

claim: Boris Johnson reportedly told colleagues he would rather 'let the bodies pile high' than impose another lockdown [26:05]
quote: he tells colleagues that he would rather let the bodies pile high than confine people to their homes again
evidence: Originally reported by the Daily Mail via unnamed sources (April 2021 reporting of an alleged October 2020 remark); No.10 and ministers denied it at the time. It was later reported to have been corroborated by testimony from a senior Johnson aide to the UK Covid Inquiry, though no single directly-linked, on-record source for that corroboration was found in this search, capping the verdict at plausible.

claim: The Conservative Party's opinion poll lead peaked at around 22% while Boris Johnson was hospitalized with COVID [26:05]
quote: the conservative party's lead in the polls which had peaked at 22% whilst Johnson was in hospital
evidence: A Survation poll taken 27-28 April 2020 (just after Johnson's 12 April discharge) put the Conservative lead at 17 points; other pollsters reported leads 'briefly surpassing 20%' in March-April 2020. 22% is within the range reported across pollsters, but no single poll matching exactly 22% during the hospitalization window itself was located.

claim: In May 2021 the Conservatives won the Hartlepool by-election, their first win there since 1959 [26:05]
quote: in May the conservatives win a historic by-election victory in Harley pool
evidence: Conservative Jill Mortimer won the 6 May 2021 by-election with a 16-point swing — the seat's first Tory MP since 1959.

claim: In November 2022, the Daily Mirror published an article revealing that Boris Johnson and his staff had hosted several parties at 10 Downing Street the previous Christmas [27:07]
quote: then it all comes crashing down in November 2022 The Daily Mirror publishes an article revealing that Boris Johnson and his staff had hosted several staff parties in 10 Downing Street the previous Christmas
evidence: The Daily Mirror's first Partygate report was published on 30 November 2021, not November 2022 — a full year off. This also creates an internal contradiction in the video's own timeline: it goes on to describe the fines (issued April 2022) and Johnson's resignation (July 2022) as following this revelation, which would be impossible if the story had broken in November 2022.

claim: In total, 17 lockdown-breaching gatherings ('Partygate') were found to have taken place, and both Boris Johnson and Rishi Sunak were fined for breaking the law [27:07]
quote: all in all 17 parties are found to have taken place among staff and both Johnson and rishy sunak are eventually fined for breaking the law
evidence: Widely reported running tally of 17 gatherings (18 counting two merged events) across the scandal, though Sue Gray's own report formally examined 16. The Met fined Johnson, his wife Carrie and Sunak over the June 2020 birthday gathering; both men's fines are confirmed and were paid.

claim: Boris Johnson attempted to promote an MP (Chris Pincher) who had been credibly accused of multiple counts of sexual assault, triggering mass resignations from his government [28:12]
quote: Johnson attempts to promote an MP who's been credibly accused of multiple accounts of sexual assault and his fellow MPS begin resigning from Johnson's government on mass
evidence: Chris Pincher was accused of groping two men on 29-30 June 2022 despite prior allegations known to Johnson; over 60 ministers/officials resigned 5-7 July 2022, the largest mass resignation in British political history.

claim: Boris Johnson's fellow MPs began resigning en masse on 'the 8th of July 2022' [28:12]
quote: on the 8th of July 2022
evidence: Mass resignations ran 5-7 July 2022, and Johnson announced he would resign as Conservative leader on 7 July 2022 — one day earlier than the claim's date of 8 July.

claim: Liz Truss was a co-author of the 2012 book 'Britannia Unchained' [29:16]
quote: a one-time contributor to a book called britania Unchained
evidence: Truss co-authored 'Britannia Unchained' (Sept 2012) with Kwasi Kwarteng, Priti Patel, Dominic Raab and Chris Skidmore.

claim: On 23 September 2022 the Truss government unveiled a package of around £45 billion in tax cuts, funded by increased borrowing [29:16-30:19]
quote: on the 23rd of September 2022 truss unveils a package of economic policies which revolve around 45 billion worth of tax cuts to the country's richest
evidence: Kwarteng's 23 September 2022 'Growth Plan' included almost £45bn/year of unfunded tax cuts — the biggest tax-cutting budget since 1972.

claim: Liz Truss resigned 49 days after taking office, becoming the shortest-serving Prime Minister in UK history [30:19]
quote: just 49 days after she first entered truss walks back out of 10 Downing Street and you guessed it resigns in doing so she becomes the shortest serving prime minister in UK history
evidence: 'Shortest-serving PM' is unambiguous. On timing: Truss became PM 6 Sept 2022, announced her resignation 20 Oct (44 days later), and formally left office when Sunak took over 25 Oct (49 days later) — the claim's '49 days' matches the day she is shown walking out of No.10 for the last time, though some outlets instead cite 44/45 days to the announcement.

claim: The Daily Star ran a livestream betting that Liz Truss would resign before a lettuce wilted, and the lettuce 'won' [30:19]
quote: the daily St posts a live stream of a lettuce on YouTube wagering that truss's failure is so bad that she'll resign before the lettuce wills and a few days later the lce claims Victory
evidence: The Daily Star's lettuce livestream began 14 October 2022; Truss resigned 20 October, before the ~10-day shelf-life of the lettuce elapsed.

claim: After Liz Truss's resignation, Labour's opinion poll lead over the Conservatives widened to around 30 points [31:22]
quote: the Gap has now widened to the point that the conservatives are a full 30 points behind
evidence: Polling around Truss's resignation showed Labour leads ranging 21-36 points across pollsters, including widely reported 30-point leads — squarely within the claim's range.

claim: Rishi Sunak became UK Prime Minister on 25 October 2022 [31:22]
quote: on the 25th of October 2022 he becomes prime minister of the UK
evidence: Sunak took over as PM on 25 October 2022, after Truss's resignation and a short leadership contest — exact match.

claim: At the start of 2023 Rishi Sunak made five pledges to the British people, and by mid-2024 the only one clearly met was bringing down inflation, credited more to falling energy prices than to government action [31:22]
quote: at the beginning of 2023 he makes five promises to the British people…the only target which actually gets met is his promise to bring down inflation but that's more to do with falling Energy prices than anything he's done himself
evidence: Institute for Government's assessment: the inflation pledge was achieved (largely via falling energy prices); the debt pledge was 'in doubt'; the small-boats pledge effectively failed; NHS waiting lists rose rather than fell; growth continued only weakly, including two negative quarters (a technical recession) in 2023. Inflation stands out as the clear success, matching the claim.

claim: After 14 years of Conservative government, more than £100 billion in cuts had been made to UK public services [32:25]
quote: after 14 years in power more than 100 billion pounds in cuts to Public Services
evidence: No single source gives an exact, aggregated 'over £100bn cut to public services' figure. IFS puts the spending-cuts share of fiscal consolidation at ~5% of GDP, which would exceed £100bn in absolute terms over the period; separately, the New Economics Foundation estimated UK GDP was £100bn lower by 2019 due to austerity — a different metric (foregone output, not direct service cuts). The order of magnitude is corroborated from two directions but the precise figure is not independently confirmed.

claim: A researcher at the Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) said the UK had developed a debilitating 'investment phobia,' where the government's reluctance to invest in infrastructure discourages business investment too [35:36]
quote: one researcher at The Institute for Public Policy suggested that the UK had contracted a debilitating case of investment phobia
evidence: IPPR's Luke Murphy used precisely this phrase ('debilitating case of investment-phobia') in IPPR's own published commentary; IPPR separately documents UK business investment as lowest in the G7.

claim: Boris Johnson texted David Cameron the day after the referendum was announced, declaring he would back the Leave campaign [13:55]
quote: Johnson declares whatever troops there might have been between them to be over and says that he'll be throwing his full weight behind the leave campaign

claim: Nebula's referral link offers 40% off an annual plan, bringing the cost to $2.50/month [38:45-39:51]
quote: that link gets you access to 40% off an annual plan so that you can watch all of that amazing stuff for just $2.50 a month
